title: Ethiopian Beef Liver Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the liver wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Gubet Wat — beef liver sliced and cooked quickly in kibbeh with onion, jalapeño, and berbere. The liver must be cooked quickly — over-cooked liver is rubbery. Done right, it is one of the most nutritious and most flavourful Ethiopian preparations.
longDesc: Liver wat is the fastest Ethiopian main dish — the liver must be cooked quickly to remain tender. The kibbeh and berbere provide the Ethiopian character; the jalapeño provides freshness and heat. Served with injera, it is one of the most nutritionally dense meals possible.
ingredients: 500g beef or calf liver — sliced 1cm thick
steps: Slice liver. Remove membrane and any tubes.
Sear liver in a single layer — 1.5 minutes per side only.
In the same pan: cook onion 2 minutes. Add jalapeño, garlic, berbere.
Return liver. Toss. Season. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Liver is done at 1.5 minutes per side — over-cooking is the only mistake.
Serve the instant it is done — waiting makes it tough.
cookingScience: Liver has very low fat content and high protein — it goes from tender to tough very quickly as the proteins denature. At 70°C internal temperature, the liver is perfectly cooked; at 80°C it becomes unpleasantly tough. The total cooking time from a hot pan to 70°C is approximately 3 minutes.
sustainabilityTips: Liver is the most nutritionally concentrated part of the animal.
healthBenefits: Liver is the world's most nutrient-dense food.
Exceptional B12, iron, vitamin A, folate.
culturalNote: Gubet Wat is the Ethiopian dish of maximum nutrition — the liver, properly cooked in one minute per side in kibbeh, provides more vitamins and minerals per gram than any other food preparation.
